Prevention: Rotate rice with vegetables as rice and other cereal crops are major hosts of paddy armyworm.
Control grassy weeds in the rice field as they are alternative hosts.
Carabid ground beetles by reducing pesticide use and growing flowering plants along border.
Apply no more than the recommended dose of nitrogen fertilizer (100 kg
N/ha) as too vigorous growth can increase armyworm infestation.
Paddy armyworm with a narrow, white dorsal line (NBAIR)
Monitoring: Use 2-5 light traps/ha at the edge of the field and examine traps weekly for moths.
After observing first moths in light traps, start monitoring the rice plants weekly to check caterpillar damage in crop (massive leaf removal, often including leaf veins) as damage occurs suddenly.
Check for stout, hairless and brown caterpillars with a narrow, white dorsal line.
During grain filling stage, the larger caterpillars cut off panicles at their base causing some to bend while others fall to the ground.
Apply control measures if 1-2 larvae/hill during pre-panicle stage and 1 larva/hill at panicle stage are observed.
Direct Control: Hand-pick egg masses (laid in single or double rows between the base of the leaf sheath and stem, which are not covered with hair) or larvae from seedbeds or a young crop and destroy them.
Flooding of the nursery bed/main field and dragging ropes across the top of the rice plants to detach and drown the larvae.
Secondary contact action but pests need to ingest it.

Use insecticides to control the larval stage.

When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing (PPE) and follow the instructions on the product label.
